_note: Picker metadata. `title` names the JOB the template does, `note` says what it holds and when it wins, `points` is how many repeating sub-items a body page takes, `needs` are HARD requirements — a family tagged screenshots is unusable without real screenshots, logos without real named tools, numbers without real figures. All three fields were derived from the templates' actual slots, not from how the pages look. A family missing here falls back to its slug and its fixture brief.

agent-lineup.title: Component roster
agent-lineup.note: One named component per page with three tools under it and a result line. Only for a system made of named parts — it has no slot for an argument. Near-black cards.

before-after.title: Before / after with figures
before-after.note: Two panes per page, a bad figure against a good one. Unusable unless the subject is a genuine before-and-after with real numbers. Warm paper, clay against green.

beige-paper.title: One paragraph per page
beige-paper.note: A title and a single paragraph. No lists, no data, no logos — the lowest-capacity prose family here. For a slow first-person reflection. Soft beige, serif, drawn swash.

black-mindmap.title: Five-pill list
black-mindmap.note: Five short pills per page and nothing else — no paragraph, no glosses. Black with a green marker. Still carries an uppercase eyebrow and a swipe arrow from the original set.

black-warning.title: Statement and callout
black-warning.note: One paragraph plus one callout per page. Almost no structure, which is the point — for blunt rules and things people get wrong. Near-white with heavy black marks.

blue-italic.title: Three figures, editorial
blue-italic.note: Three figure-and-label pairs plus a paragraph and a strip line. Needs real numbers. Pale stone, a half-circle bleeding off one edge, italic accent.

bold-split.title: Three figures, split panel
bold-split.note: Three figure-and-label pairs and a paragraph. Needs real numbers. Ink on cream cut by a deep angled slate panel — stronger diagonal than the other figure families.

claude-target.title: Three-step method
claude-target.note: Three titled steps per page, each with one line under it. No figures or tools required. For a method or sequence. Saturated colour mesh with one drawn object.

condensed-pill.title: Time saved per tactic
condensed-pill.note: One tactic per page with a savings figure and two tool marks. Needs both to work. Built specifically for hours-back subjects. Warm paper, one solid pill.

coral-mag.title: Three figures, magazine
coral-mag.note: Three figure pairs, a paragraph and one named tool. Needs numbers and a tool worth naming. Coral mesh, large editorial display.

cream-3d.title: Three figures and a tip
cream-3d.note: Three figure pairs, a paragraph and a separate tip block, with one named tool. Needs numbers. Cool stone gradient, terracotta accent, very large type.

cream-best.title: Tool shortlist
cream-best.note: One headline figure and one tile per page over a logo row. Only for a shortlist where the tools themselves are the subject. Cream and green meshes.

cream-claude.title: Three blocks with metrics
cream-claude.note: Three titled blocks, each carrying its own metric, plus four tool marks. Needs a figure per block. Cream mesh with a terracotta strip.

cream-desk.title: Screenshot and use metric
cream-desk.note: One real product screenshot per page with the tool name, a use metric and a note. Unusable without actual screenshots. Bright cream, screen set flat.

cream-gold.title: Three pillars and a price
cream-gold.note: Three pillars, a price figure and a pull quote. Needs a number worth naming out loud — built for rates and money. Cream with a single gold bar.

cream-notes.title: Annotated screenshot
cream-notes.note: One real screenshot per page annotated with three short lines. Unusable without actual screenshots. For showing a setup rather than describing it. Cream, margin-note feel.

cream-shots.title: Screenshot and statement
cream-shots.note: One real screenshot per page under a large statement, plus a use metric. The cleanest of the screenshot set. Cream, screen held square in the frame.

cream-slab.title: Screenshot, captioned
cream-slab.note: One real screenshot per page with a single caption line — the least copy of the screenshot set apart from cream-tilt. Cream with a dark slab behind the screen.

cream-table.title: Compatibility table
cream-table.note: Two use blocks with metrics over a five-logo compatibility row. For what a tool works with, not what it does. Cream mesh with docked tiles.

cream-tilt.title: Screenshot, no copy
cream-tilt.note: One real screenshot per page with a tool name and tagline and nothing else. The lowest text capacity in the set. Cream, device tilted and bleeding off frame.

dark-blob.title: Three figures, dark
dark-blob.note: Three figure pairs and a paragraph with one named tool. Needs numbers. Near-black with a hot orange mass per page — the loudest of the dark figure families.

dark-green-serif.title: Three points, serif
dark-green-serif.note: Three titled points and a paragraph. No figures required. Reflective register — good for the parts of a job nobody writes down. Deep green-black, mint, serif display.

dark-navy.title: Three figures and an insight
dark-navy.note: Three figure pairs, a paragraph and a separate insight line. Needs numbers. Navy proportional bands with a filled panel closing the foot.

dark-pill-glow.title: Two-sided comparison
dark-pill-glow.note: A left/right pill pair with a value on each side. Very compact and needs a genuinely two-sided figure. Very dark blue with a cool blue accent.

data-table.title: Four-bar chart
data-table.note: Four labelled bars with percentages and values in their own column. Completely unusable without real quantities. Paper with a blue accent.

design-tile.title: Right against wrong
design-tile.note: Three wrong practices set against three right ones, each side with a claim. Only for subjects that split cleanly in two. Cool grey with teal tiles.

edu-bright.title: Chart, flow and table
edu-bright.note: Its body pages are three different shapes — a five-bar chart, a flow and a table. Needs real figures. For explaining how something works and where it breaks. Warm off-white, amber.

ember-dark.title: Three figures, monochrome
ember-dark.note: Three figure pairs, a paragraph and an insight line, centred on one mark. Needs numbers. Near-black run monochrome in bone — no second colour anywhere.

flowchart.title: Decision tree
flowchart.note: A root question splitting into two branches with a card under each. Only for a real either/or — it cannot hold three options. Pale lilac, violet, drawn flow.

grid-italic.title: Three metrics and bullets
grid-italic.note: Three metrics plus three bullets and a paragraph. Needs numbers. Warm paper, deep red, a ruled grid with italic display — old-print feel.

highlight-box.title: Three facts, highlighted
highlight-box.note: Three facts each carrying a metric, plus one statement with a highlighted clause. Needs a figure per fact. Black with acid yellow as the only colour.

indigo-mag.title: Three figures and a named tool
indigo-mag.note: Three figure pairs, a paragraph, and one tool with its role spelled out. Needs numbers. Indigo mesh with a stat dock along the foot.

leak-dark.title: Three blocks, dark
leak-dark.note: Three titled blocks and a subtitle. No figures required. Cold and forensic — suits things that only break once real users arrive. Almost pure black, pale cyan.

lime-accent.title: Calendar week
lime-accent.note: Three rows read against a calendar grid, plus a takeaway. Only for something genuinely scheduled — a launch week, a sprint. Near-black with a lime wedge.

linkedin-pro.title: Four-paragraph essay
linkedin-pro.note: Four paragraphs, a standfirst and a pull line. Prose, not lists — no figure or logo slots at all. The most conservative family here. Grey paper, navy, serif display.

mag-editorial.title: Magazine feature
mag-editorial.note: Two columns with a dropcap, a quote and three margin notes. The highest word count in the set. For a long argued piece. Cream spread with hairlines.

minimal-beauty.title: Three points and a pull quote
minimal-beauty.note: Three titled points and a pull quote. No data, no logos, very little on the page. Pick it when restraint is itself the argument. Warm putty, type and space.

mint-condensed.title: Two points, condensed
mint-condensed.note: Three body lines and two titled points — deliberately low capacity. For attention, focus, saying less. Pale mint-grey with condensed display type.

mono-pattern.title: In / act / out flow
mono-pattern.note: Two notes plus a three-part input-action-output flow. For a small mechanical process with a clear shape. Warm paper, rust, a repeating field as texture.

noir-yellow.title: Three points, no imagery
noir-yellow.note: Three titled points, two display lines and a closing line. Nothing drawn anywhere. Hard and adult — built for negotiating, money and refusal. Black and gold.

paper-fold.title: Two points, light
paper-fold.note: Two titled points and a paragraph. Deliberately sparse — do not force a third. For instructions and briefs. Warm paper folded, forest green.

pastel-soft.title: Two points and a pull line
pastel-soft.note: Two titled points and a pull line. Gentle register; suits persistence and slow subjects. Lilac-white with soft shapes held out at the corners.

personal-essay.title: Two-paragraph essay
personal-essay.note: Two paragraphs and a pull line — prose only, no list slots at all. The most first-person family here. Warm gradient with contour drawings, serif display.

photo-split.title: Three rows and a gauge
photo-split.note: Three key/value rows plus a percentage gauge and an aside. Needs one real figure for the gauge. For decisions made without enough information. Cold slate against sand.

photo-tag.title: Four captioned plates
photo-tag.note: Four captioned plates per page, each with a real gloss — one of the highest item counts here. For a set of methods. Off-white grid, one plate raised in purple.

pixel-block.title: One figure, in blocks
pixel-block.note: Two points and a single headline figure drawn as blocks. Needs something countable. For estimates and whole numbers. Pale grey with a red accent.

purple-mist.title: Three points, orbit
purple-mist.note: Three titled points and a paragraph. No data required. Deep aubergine with tilted ellipses stroked and never filled, kept clear of the type.

retro-groovy.title: Three points, informal
retro-groovy.note: Three titled points and a paragraph. Loosest register of the three-point families. Sand and burnt orange with curved shapes at the edges.

rounded-card.title: Three plates, product
rounded-card.note: Three captioned plates and a paragraph. Product-flavoured without needing screenshots. For first impressions and onboarding. Cool grey, slate blue, soft corners.

second-brain.title: Three points, filed
second-brain.note: Three titled points under a filing tab. For systems, notes and anything meant to survive being left alone. Warm paper with olive.

shout-orange.title: One statement per page
shout-orange.note: A title, an accent phrase and one paragraph. Nothing else fits — the lowest capacity and the highest impact in the set. A flooded orange page, type at maximum size.

stack-tour.title: Three layers
stack-tour.note: Three key/value pairs read top to bottom as layers, plus a paragraph. Only for genuinely layered subjects. Cold slate with a pale blue accent.

stencil-stamp.title: Three points and a stamp
stencil-stamp.note: Three titled points plus a two-line stamp phrase per page. Paper with crop marks, a registration frame and one band inked red. Suits process and approval subjects.

swiss-grid.title: Three points, Swiss grid
swiss-grid.note: Three key/value pairs and a long paragraph set narrow — it wants more words than the other three-point families. Strict six-column grid with visible hairlines, white and one red.

teal-mag.title: Three figures, teal
teal-mag.note: Three figure pairs, a paragraph and one named tool with its role. Needs numbers. Teal mesh with a stat dock — the brightest of the magazine families.

tech-stack-grid.title: Six-cell taxonomy
tech-stack-grid.note: Six paired cells per page — the highest item count in the set. Keep the same six angles on every page or it stops reading as a taxonomy. Near-black and pale gold, no logos.

terminal-glow.title: Three points, phosphor
terminal-glow.note: Three key/value pairs and a paragraph. True black with scan lines as the ground and one register lit green. No terminal chrome, so it suits method rather than code.

terracotta.title: Three points, punched
terracotta.note: Three key/value pairs and a paragraph. Two flat fields split hard with perfect circles punched through both. No shadows, no gradients — cut paper.

tool-list.title: Four-item checklist
tool-list.note: Four hanging entries and a paragraph — more items per page than the three-point families. Paper and deep olive, everything hung off one line, no boxes at all.

typo-sample.title: Type specimen
typo-sample.note: One enormous phrase per page over three small key/value notes. The phrase does all the work, so it has to be short and good. Black on white only, no third colour.

wine-mag.title: Three figures, wine
wine-mag.note: Three figure pairs, a paragraph and one named tool with its role. Needs numbers. Wine mesh with a pink accent — the warmest magazine family.

y2k-window.title: Four-cell grid
y2k-window.note: Four paired cells in a two-by-two grid. Silver bevelled chrome plates, one inverted per page. No window chrome, so it reads as machined rather than as a desktop.
